issues.description: The Meal constructor parameter order in the template does not match the problem statement UML and the solution. The problem statement and solution expect Meal(String name, String[] ingredients), but the template's Meal constructor is defined as Meal(String[] ingredients, String name). This also contradicts the example usage in Main which calls new Meal("cowBoyStew", new String[]{...}) and would not compile against the template constructor signature, causing confusion and compilation errors for students following the instructions.
issues.suggestedFix: Change the Meal constructor in the template to match the specification and solution: public Meal(String name, String[] ingredients). Alternatively, update the example usages in Main to use the template's parameter order. Preferably align the template constructor with the problem statement and solution to avoid student confusion.

issues.description: The problem statement (and the solution) define the Meal constructor as Meal(String name, String[] ingredients), but the template's Meal class declares the constructor with the parameter order reversed (Meal(String[] ingredients, String name)). This causes a mismatch with the examples in Main (which call new Meal("name", new String[]{...})) and with the class diagram in the problem description, creating compilation errors and cognitive mapping confusion for students trying to map the requirement to the provided template.
issues.suggestedFix: Change the template Meal constructor signature to match the problem statement and solution: public Meal(String name, String[] ingredients) and assign this.name = name; this.ingredients = ingredients;. Alternatively, update the example usages in Main to use the template's current parameter order, but aligning the template to the problem/solution (name first) is recommended.
